title: Data Mapping & Verification Playbook — Compliance Messaging (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is intended for sellers, solutions engineers, and GTM content owners to quickly translate product telemetry and architectural controls into repeatable evidence narratives for SOC2, ISO, and HIPAA diligence. Focus: practical mapping from customer questions (DDQs) to the smallest verifiable artifact we can provide with low friction (logs, config screenshots, audited statements).

Audience:
- Enterprise AE/CSE preparing an evaluation call
- Security reviewer doing an initial DDQ
- Presales engineer building a tailored evidence package

High-level guidance (one-liner):
- Surface the exact ask, map to an evidence type, and attach the narrowest artifact (e.g., "audit-log for X: sample query + 7-day slice") rather than broad assertions.
- Use immutable artifacts whenever possible (signed PDFs, KMS-backed key rotation logs, signed SOC2 report pages).
- When live system access is required, provide sanitized, time-boxed examples and a reproducible query so the customer can validate without exposing additional data.

Core claim categories and evidence patterns:
1) Data residency & locality claims
   - Common asks: where data is stored, where inference occurs, transfer across regions
   - Evidence types: S3 bucket location config screenshot, VPC routing table snippet, cloud-region labels on deployment manifest, sample request id with region label
   - Seller script: "We pin inference to region X by default; here's a deployment manifest and an S3 location screenshot showing data-at-rest in eu-west-1."

2) Audit logging & tamper-resistance
   - Common asks: retention, write-once, access controls, ingestion pipeline
   - Evidence types: sample audit-log export (redacted), the script used to produce the export, cloud object immutability policy, KMS key usage logs showing write operations
   - Suggested operational proof: provide a reproducible query (timestamp range + user id pattern) and a 3-entry log slice with associated signatures/hash where applicable.

3) Access control & least privilege
   - Common asks: who can view customer data, role definitions, break-glass procedures
   - Evidence types: IAM role list screenshot, least-privilege RBAC policy snippet, an e-mail template for break-glass approvals, an audit of a temporary access grant (redacted)

4) Key management and encryption
   - Common asks: customer-managed keys (CMK), rotation cadence, HSM usage
   - Evidence types: KMS key policy snippet, key-rotation log entry, HSM attestation doc or vendor summary page

5) Operational readiness & incident response
   - Common asks: incident playbooks, MTTD/MTTR metrics, escalation matrix
   - Evidence types: incident timeline redaction, postmortem summary with blameless root cause and remediation, runbook extract showing detection rules

Evidence packaging conventions (reduce friction)
- Name artifacts with: claim-shortname_customer-friendly-date (e.g., auditlog-generation-2024-10-01).
- Include a one-line provenance header in each artifact: who generated it, what tool, time range, and the Jira/Confluence reference.
- Prefer sample slices with explicit redaction markers (<<REDACTED>>) and an explanation of what was removed.
- For logs, include the query used to extract the slice and the CLI command.

Example: Audit-log sample deliverable- File: auditlog-s3-object-events-2024-10-01.txt- Header: "Generated by observability-export v1.3; query: SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE customer_id='<<REDACTED>>' AND service='inference' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-09-25' AND '2024-10-01'"- Content: three redacted events showing write, read, and key-usage; include event ids and hash footers if available

Competitive notes (how to differentiate):
- Competitor A: publishes high-level compliance summaries but lacks reproducible log exports; our advantage: reproducible, queryable slices and the extraction scripts.
- Competitor B: offers on-prem bundles with full logs but requires long professional services; our advantage: self-serve sanitized exports + scripted provenance for fast evals.
- Differentiation messaging to use: "We deliver reproducible, timeboxed evidence artifacts so security teams can validate controls without a full audit or long PS engagement."

Seller Q&A snippets (short scripts)
- Customer: "Can you show me how audit logs are structured?"
  Seller: "Yes — we'll provide a 7-day sample export and the exact query plus the CLI command we used. That lets your team run the same extraction in a sandbox if you want."
- Customer: "How long are logs retained?"
  Seller: "Default retention is 90 days for audit events; we offer extended retention add-ons and can show retention config in the logging bucket policy."

Risk & mitigations (for internal reviewers)
- Risk: Customers request full-live access to raw logs.
  Mitigation: Offer reproducible slices, recorded extraction steps, and a short signed attestation from SRE that the extraction was limited.
- Risk: Customers with extremely long retention requirements (7+ years).
  Mitigation: Standard add-on packaging with cost estimate + architecture note (cold storage archival).

Open questions / follow-ups- Should we standardize a single sandbox query library for the most common DDQ asks? (proposal: yes — owner: Priya D.)- Legal needs a templated attestation statement for exported artifacts. (owner: Jon C.)- Investigate automating the export + redaction pipeline as a small internal tool (ticket: GTMS-1123).

Next steps (90-day plan)
1) Finalize 10 canonical export queries and add to Confluence (owner: Mateo).
2) Create 3 example artifacts per claim category and a short one-slide evidence cheat sheet (owner: Asha).
3) Build a one-click export script prototype that records provenance (owner: Eng: Lin Wu, ticket GTMS-1123).

Appendix — quick checklist for package assembly
- Identify exact DDQ item and map to one of the claim categories above
- Choose smallest artifact that proves the claim (config screenshot, 3-line log slice, signed doc)
- Run export, add header + provenance, redact sensitive fields, store in restricted Confluence folder, note link in email to customer
- Close loop in Jira with customer touchpoint and internal evidence id

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep artifacts lean — security teams prefer reproducible samples over huge dumps.
- We should pilot this playbook with 2 current enterprise trials this quarter and measure time-to-deliver evidence (target <48h).
- Attachments to prepare: sample audit exports (s3, keystorage), IAM policy snippets, retention policy screenshot.

Document history:
- Drafted 2024-08-12 by A. Patel
- Comments incorporated 2024-10-15 (Mateo, Lin)
- Current review 2024-11-02: finalize templates and owner assignments

End of playbook.
